newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. developer blames Israel for suicide attack.
newsitem.headline: U.S. developer blames Israel for suicide attack.

text.p: A U.S. Jewish businessman who bankrolls Jewish settlements said Israel's hesitation to build his project in Arab East Jerusalem "encouraged" suicide bombers who killed 13 people at an Israeli street market.

"Our lack of ability to stand by our right to build in East Jerusalem encourages them to commit suicide attacks like that," Irving Moskowitz told the newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth in an interview published on Friday. "They see us hesitate."
A leaflet issued in the name of the Islamic militant group Hamas claimed responsibility for Wednesday's attack by two suicide bombers in Jewish west Jerusalem's main market.

The Miami magnate, who received a permit to build for Jews in East Jerusalem's Ras al-Amoud neighbourhood last week, said he was surprised by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's vow to block the project for now.
"When the government blocks legal construction and gives in to pressure, that signals them that we are weak," he said.
"I thought Bibi would support (me)," said Moskowitz, using Netanyahu's nickname. "He knows what I do in East Jerusalem and he knows about my involvement over the years."
Moskowitz said he had backed Netanyahu since the 1970s.
"I was not among his first supporters. I was his only supporter," the businessman said, adding that he had helped finance Netanyahu's 1996 election campaign.
Moskowitz said that he had heard Saudi Arabia might want to buy the Ras al-Amoud plot. He said he might like to buy land in the holy Moslem city of Mecca in the Gulf state.
Asked under what conditions he might give up the project or sell the site, he said: "I heard Saudi Arabia wants to acquire it. That's interesting. I want to buy in Mecca."
Israel's Interior Ministry on Monday suspended the Ras al- Amoud plan until an appeal by leftist members of Israel's Jerusalem city council against the 70-home project is heard on Tuesday.
Palestinians had warned the construction would bury peace moves. Netanyahu said that while he supported building anywhere in Jerusalem, now was not the time for Ras al-Amoud.

Israel occupied Arab East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war. It vows never to cede an inch of the city. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state. They say building for Jews there pre-empts final peace talks.
